dogecoin.text:
@DevavratDR @poppeyrs @trungduca8hn @scottmelker If it is faster it's probably less decentralized. If it's faster it probably has big blocks, which makes it heavier and harder to run, contributing to network centralization.

Dogecoin has a problem, it depends on Elon Musk. That's a bug, not a feature.

@DevavratDR @poppeyrs @trungduca8hn @scottmelker Miners don't secure the network. Nodes do. Miners propose blocks, Nodes accept them or reject them.

So even if out of nowhere the hash rate of Dogecoin would increase, you'd still be lacking a huge network of Nodes that validate those blocks and secure the blockchain.
